key_insight: Thermal insulation can relax the need to prevent carrier-to-lattice energy transfer, while absorber ohmic heat can be partially recycled into electrical work at the Carnot efficiency factor.
engineering_relevance: The analysis identifies absorber thermal insulation, energy-selective contacts, and low contact heat leakage as design targets for high-efficiency hot-carrier and hot-absorber solar cells.
method: Analyze thermally insulated absorbers with carrier-to-lattice energy transfer.
Include ohmic losses from finite absorber electrical conductivity.
Evaluate sensitivity to finite contact-mediated heat leakage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports thermodynamic-limit analysis and heat-leakage sensitivity results, not experimental validation or practical device-efficiency projections.
watch_item: High efficiency depends on ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance, which remain demanding implementation requirements.
paper_title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
